analysis.title: We Are Getting Lots Of Client Pushback Against Our Call To "Embrace Risk"
key_insights: Morgan Stanley chief economist Seth Carpenter reports heavy client pushback at the Asia Pacific Summit in Singapore against the 'Embracing Risk' strategy title, driven by the global equity overweight recommendation.
Equities continued to sell off on the Friday after the conference ended, which Carpenter says highlights investor concerns.
MS is constructive on growth. US growth is driven by AI capex and household spending, and AI-driven wealth gains support consumption, so less conviction in AI would mean less confidence in growth.
The AI story is global, as US capex fuels Asian exports, and MS thinks the Asian capex cycle is broadening and becoming self-sustaining beyond AI.
MS has less conviction in its inflation forecast. It expects inflation to peak in Q1 next year and then retreat gradually, so DM central banks would hike less than markets currently price.

If wrong, inflation is more likely to surprise higher than lower. An energy-shock-driven rise with tighter policy and a growth slump is risk negative, while demand-driven inflation with pricing power would be a boon for equities.
The path to end-2027 is expected to be bumpy. Upside inflation surprises could trigger further repricing of policy expectations and higher rates.
Risks include geopolitics, a possible US government shutdown or debt limit episode, and worldwide elections, especially in France where the fiscal path has moved sovereign debt markets.
The message is 'embrace risk', not 'relax, the worst is over', and MS lays out bull and bear scenarios across asset classes and economic risk scenarios.

macro_indicators.reading: peak in Q1 next year then gradual retreat
macro_indicators.interpretation: If MS is right, DM central banks hike less than market pricing, which supports equities. Risk skews to higher inflation.

risk_factors: Inflation surprising to the upside, causing further repricing of monetary policy and higher rates.
Energy shock combined with tighter monetary policy causing a growth slump.
Reduced conviction in the AI story would weaken capex and household wealth-driven spending.
US government shutdown or debt limit episode.
French elections and fiscal path pressuring sovereign debt markets.
vol_and_positioning: Equities continued to sell off on Friday after the conference ended, reflecting investor concern about the overweight equity call.
geopolitical: Geopolitical risk is described as not going away even with a divided US government after the midterms.
Fiscal sustainability concerns include a possible US government shutdown or debt limit episode and elections worldwide, especially in France.

tension_points.bull_case: Growth stays solid on AI capex and household spending, and sticky inflation is unlikely to derail the trend. Demand-driven inflation with pricing power would boost nominal earnings.
tension_points.bear_case: Clients push back as equities sold off. Inflation has surprised upward, rates could rise further, and an energy shock plus tight policy could cause a growth slump.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An energy-shock-driven inflation overshoot combined with tighter monetary policy causing a growth slump, or reduced conviction in the AI capex story.

theme_stances.key_argument: The vast majority of evidence says growth stays solid and sticky inflation probably will not be sufficient to derail the trend.
theme_stances.evidence: we are saying “embrace risk,” not “relax, the worst is over.”

theme_stances.key_argument: AI capex and AI-driven household wealth underpin US growth, and the Asian capex cycle is broadening beyond AI.
theme_stances.evidence: a lot of the growth is driven by AI capex along with continued spending by households
